note: Woodbury County Conservation park on Snyder Bend Lake, an oxbow of the Missouri River cut off when the river was channelized in the early 1960s, 3 mi west of Salix. The camping loops fill the park's north-west end above the lake-shore trail; boat ramp, accessible fishing dock, half-mile paved trail and a waterfowl observation deck. The adjoining wildlife refuge is closed to all entry September 10 - December 25. --Claude

WATERFRONT (lakeview kept): Snyder Bend Lake is a Missouri River oxbow ~150 m wide and several hundred metres long here (far over 5 acres). On imagery and the county's park map, the pads are spurs on the inside of the camp loop road; the loop road and then the paved lake-shore trail run between the westernmost pads and the water (~30-60 m, open lawn with scattered trees). Road + trail in between = *view at best; the lake is visible across open ground, so lakeview.
